evidence: Plin. NH 11.238: omne lac igne spissātur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Pliny’s words for milk thickened over the fire. Condensed milk is milk boiled down, usually with sugar; the product is modern, and the name, from Pliny’s phrase, is ours. Where the sweetness matters, lac spissātum dulce.
A description of ours: dēcoquere is the verb for boiling a liquid down to a part of itself (Varro, Columella, in Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: Open the tin of condensed milk.

phrases.latin: Lac spissātum dulce est tamquam mel.
phrases.english: Condensed milk is as sweet as honey.

sources: Lewis & Short: spisso · Lewis & Short: decoquo
